newsitem.title: DUBAI: Oman says Israeli links not against Arab interest.
newsitem.headline: Oman says Israeli links not against Arab interest.

text.p: An Omani cabinet minister said that it was in the interest of Arab states to have links with Israel, which would then be convinced of the importance of peace.

"There is an Arab point of view (which opposes rushing into normalising ties with Israel)...which we respect, appreciate and understand...," said Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Youssef bin Alawi bin Abdullah in an interview with the London-based al-Hayat newspaper.

"But there is another view that we have to encourage Israel (by showing) that it has an interest in peace and this interest comes from having links with the Arab world," he said in the Wednesday edition.
"We don't think that having any kind of relationship or contacts (with Israel) is against the Arab interest, on the contrary it is in the Arab's interest," he said.

Abdullah also argued that right-wing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had shifted his views on the peace process since taking office in June. Netanyahu was elected on a platform opposed to trading occupied Arab land for peace and opposed to a Palestinian state.
"To be in the opposition is one thing and to be the government that has to abide by agreements is another...It (the Israeli government) is not today what it was yesterday."
Oman and Qatar have forged ahead of other Gulf states in establishing economic ties with Israel, but have stopped short of full diplomatic relations.
